entities.summary: Philologus of Sinope was a Seventy Disciple and a revered figure in the early Christian Church. Born in the city of Sinope, a major center of early Christian pilgrimage, he was one of the Seventy Apostles appointed by Jesus Christ. Philologus played a significant role in the dissemination of Christian teachings and the spread of the faith throughout the Mediterranean world. He is commemorated on January 4 and November 5, and his legacy continues to inspire devotion and scholarship among Christians today. His writings, although now lost, were likely influential in shaping the theological debates of the early Church. As a member of the Seventy Disciples, Philologus of Sinope was part of a network of early Christian leaders who traveled extensively, preaching and teaching the Gospel to diverse audiences. His travels took him to cities such as Jerusalem, Antioch, and Rome, where he engaged with local churches and Christian communities. Through his ministry, Philologus helped to establish the Christian Church in the East and played a key role in shaping the theology and practices of the early Christian communities. His significance extends beyond his own lifetime, as his teachings and writings helped to shape the development of Christian doctrine and practice in the centuries that followed.
